ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a large gray disk, with 13 small white circles placed inside. The small circles are arranged in a symmetric triangular lattice: 1 at the very top, 1 at the very bottom, a middle horizontal row of 3, and one row of 4 each above and below. The contacts between the small circles and between the outer small circles and the large circle are all shown as tangent, and the gray shaded region is the part inside the large circle but outside all the small circles. Reasoning: The radius of each small circle is 1, so the distance between the centers of two tangent small circles is 2. Let the center of the central small circle be the origin. According to the triangular lattice arrangement, the outer centers can be taken as (0, 2√3), (3, √3), (3, -√3), (0, -2√3), etc., and their distances to the origin are all 2√3. The large circle is tangent to these outermost small circles, so the radius of the large circle is R = 2√3 + 1. Since the 13 small circles do not overlap with each other and only touch at tangent points, the shaded area is the area of the large circle minus the area of 13 unit circles: πR^2 - 13π = π(2√3 + 1)^2 - 13π = π(13 + 4√3) - 13π = 4π√3.
